disposition_mapping.rationale: Extraction and FX retranslation become an automated, schedule-triggered pipeline with a named exception owner, satisfying ACR-R-01 and ACR-R-07 by making the risk-rated schedule and closing rate the literal trigger and tool input. Kept as its own step, not fused with matching, per the council's near-unanimous rejection of maximalist's single-pipeline fusion (agentic_architect, hitl_designer, finance_domain, emerging_economy, accounting_standards): extraction failures (missing feed, stale rate) are a different failure domain from matching-rule misses and need an independently inspectable log. A first-class manual/template-upload ingestion path is retained per emerging_economy and finance_domain's concession, not treated as a deprecated fallback. FX differences are surfaced as a distinct output per KB-08, satisfying accounting_standards' hold that a fused artifact must still be inspectable at the translation boundary.

Matching survives (ACR-R-02) as an automated rules engine with an explicit, named exception queue carrying match-confidence and rule metadata (hitl_designer's and finance_domain's refinement), rather than the ambiguous 'manual otherwise' of the baseline. Kept separate from extraction for the reasons given above. Intercompany matching is called out explicitly per KB-14 (finance_domain), and a low-cost/in-house manual matching path is preserved as first-class per emerging_economy's non-negotiable, since mandating a single commercial engine would create a two-tier control environment across the group.

Investigation and classification survives unchanged in substance (ACR-R-03), consistent with near-total council convergence (finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, accounting_standards, and maximalist's own retraction of the T2 fusion). AI assistance is permitted as a copilot that proposes explanations, but the accountable classification decision stays with the human GL accountant per KB-02's evidential-trail requirement and KB-04's estimation-judgment principle — this is explicitly not folded into matching (which would hide judgment inside a system queue) or into JE preparation (which would blur 'what happened' from 'what we'll do about it').

JE preparation survives (ACR-R-04) and continues to consume the prior-period error record (ACR-R-06, KB-05). Merged with ACR-05 into one step because the preparer and the sign-off actor are the same person, and ACR-R-05's separation requirement constrains preparer vs. reviewer, not preparer vs. self-attestation — a position reached independently by pragmatist, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, accounting_standards and (conditionally) finance_domain and emerging_economy. The step is structurally bifurcated into mechanical and estimation-entry sub-paths per finance_domain's refinement (accepted by nearly every member in round 2), so judgment-bearing entries cannot move at the speed of trivial reclasses and retain the documented basis KB-04/KB-10 require.

Sign-off is explicitly flagged unconstrained by design, and the council converged (pragmatist, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, accounting_standards, finance_domain, and emerging_economy's revised position) on preserving its substance as a discrete, gated, individually-attributed logged attestation inside the merged preparation step, rejecting maximalist's framing of it as an ambient by-product inferred from the journal simply being posted. This satisfies the cross-entity/BPO accountability concern (emerging_economy, finance_domain) via a structural submit-for-review lock rather than a second workflow hop performed by the identical actor, which would add a queue without a new check.

Reviewer approval survives for every reconciliation (ACR-R-09), performed by the finance controller as an actor structurally distinct from the T4 preparer (ACR-R-05). The council majority (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, accounting_standards) rejected maximalist's and agentic_architect's tiered auto-clear-with-sampling model: KB-02's evidential-trail principle requires a reviewer-of-record for the specific balance reported, not a statistical proxy over a population, and a sampling regime means a defined set of reconciliations is never looked at by anyone before reporting. The synthesis adopts the majority reading — review intensity is risk-weighted (AI risk-scoring directs attention, full visibility into preparer rationale per hitl_designer's sharpening) but review existence is universal and non-negotiable.

Although flagged unconstrained by design, the council converged 5-of-7 (finance_domain, emerging_economy, pragmatist, hitl_designer, accounting_standards) against folding escalation into reviewer approval's exception queue, against maximalist's and agentic_architect's proposed absorption. Ageing detection is automated and continuous, but the escalation decision and resolution ownership remain a distinct, named human accountability held by the finance controller, kept separate from sign-off approval because it is a differently-timed judgment (resolving a stuck item versus accepting a reconciliation) whose silent merger is precisely how aged items stop receiving attention — reinforcing KB-03 cutoff discipline and KB-05's non-suppression-of-errors principle.

Evidence retention and status reporting survive as a named step with explicit, inspectable outputs (ACR-R-08), rejecting maximalist's initial proposal to dissolve retention into an ambient 'system property' — a retraction maximalist itself made in round 2 after pragmatist's and accounting_standards' objection that logs must be a defined, retrievable package, not an implicit claim. Capture is automated at the point each upstream action occurs (reducing manual filing risk), but the evidence package remains portable/exportable per emerging_economy's non-negotiable (not locked to one vendor platform), and the status report remains a human-composed or human-reviewed deliverable a controller can actually read before sign-off.

steps.actor: GL accountant (extraction exception owner), automated extraction/retranslation engine
steps.description: GL and comparison balances (bank, subledger, third party) are pulled for every in-scope account on its risk-rated schedule, via an automated feed/API path where source systems support it and a first-class manual template-upload path where they do not. Foreign-currency balances are retranslated at the closing rate using a defined, auditable rate source (a live feed or a published reference rate are equally acceptable). Every run writes an immutable, inspectable log (source, timestamp, rate used, record count), and FX revaluation differences are carried forward as a distinct, separately identified output rather than folded into a generic variance. A named GL accountant owns the exception queue for missing feeds, stale rates, or accounts that fail extraction.
inputs: Reconciliation schedule by account risk rating
steps.name: Automated balance extraction and FX retranslation

steps.actor: GL accountant (matching exception owner), automated/manual matching engine
steps.description: Deterministic rules-based matching runs against the extracted balances, closing automatically wherever rules allow; items the rules cannot close are routed to an explicit, named exception queue showing match confidence and the rule that fired, not a bare pass/fail flag. Intercompany lines are matched to identifiable counterparty entries and must net to zero, never absorbed into a residual. A manual matching path (low-cost/in-house rules, not a single licensed vendor dependency) is maintained as a first-class route, not a deprecated fallback, for entities without system-integrated feeds. Kept as a separate step from extraction because the two are different failure domains (data availability vs. rule calibration) and need independently inspectable logs.
steps.name: Automated transaction matching with exception queue
outputs: Unmatched items with match-confidence and rule metadata

steps.description: Unmatched items are investigated, explained, evidenced and classified by a human GL accountant. An AI copilot may pull supporting documentation and propose a likely explanation/classification from historical patterns, but it is advisory only: the accountable human confirms or overrides every classification before it flows downstream. This step is not merged into matching or into adjustment preparation, because it is the one place the 'why' of a break is established and auditors test precisely this distinction.
inputs: Unmatched items with match-confidence and rule metadata
steps.name: Investigate and classify reconciling items
outputs: Explained and classified reconciling items with evidence

steps.description: Adjusting entries are drafted and certified by the same accountable preparer, organized into two structurally distinct sub-paths: (a) mechanical corrections (reclasses, FX true-ups, small timing differences) which the system drafts and the preparer confirms quickly, and (b) estimation-based entries (provisions, impairments, NRV write-downs) which require the preparer to enter and certify a documented basis before the entry can proceed. Prior-period errors are corrected retrospectively using the prior-period error record, never netted into the current period. Sign-off is preserved as an explicit, gated, individually attributed attestation action (a 'submit for review' lock distinct from drafting/editing) that the JE batch cannot bypass, rather than an inference from the entry simply existing. Sign-off is merged into this step because the same actor performs both and ACR-R-05 constrains preparer vs. reviewer separation, not preparer vs. self-attestation.
inputs: Explained and classified reconciling items with evidence
steps.name: Prepare and certify adjusting journal entries

steps.description: An independent finance controller reviews and approves every reconciliation and its adjusting entries before the balance is reported — no reconciliation closes without an identifiable reviewer act, regardless of materiality or how cleanly it auto-matched. Review depth, not review existence, scales with risk: an AI risk-scoring pass surfaces unusual items, large or judgment-based adjustments, and policy-inconsistent entries to focus the controller's attention, and the reviewer sees the underlying investigation rationale and preparer basis directly, not an aggregated 'all green' dashboard. Periodic sampling may run as a secondary detective layer but never substitutes for the per-reconciliation reviewer act. The reviewer is structurally distinct from the T4 preparer and holds sole approval authority; no automated agent may approve on its own or another agent's behalf.
inputs: Explained and classified reconciling items with evidence
steps.name: Risk-weighted reviewer approval

steps.description: Open reconciling items are continuously scanned against ageing thresholds and automatically flagged the moment they cross; detection is mechanical and system-generated. The escalation decision — how, to whom, and with what urgency, plus ownership of the resolution timeline — remains a distinct human judgment held by the finance controller. Kept as its own step, separate from reviewer approval, because it is a differently-timed, differently-scoped judgment (resolving something stuck versus accepting a reconciliation as reported) and folding it into approval is how aged items stop getting examined, especially for accounts that otherwise close cleanly.
steps.name: Aging-triggered escalation and resolution tracking

steps.description: Evidence from every prior step (extraction logs, match results, investigation notes, certified entries, attestations, approvals, escalations) is captured automatically at the point each action occurs and compiled into a defined, retrievable, portable (exportable, non-proprietary) evidence package per reconciliation — not an implicit claim that logs exist somewhere. Status reporting to stakeholders remains a genuine, human-reviewed deliverable: the GL accountant composes or confirms the narrative report (which accounts are late, which escalations are open, which adjustments carry estimation uncertainty) before distribution, rather than relying on a mechanically generated list alone.
steps.name: Evidence retention and status reporting
